text:
Maya: heads-up — we pushed the sidecar env config tweak to canary (v2.3.1) ~30m ago and dashboards show p95 for /generate jumped from ~120ms to ~420ms on that canary cohort. p99 up to ~900ms. Not seeing errors, just latency. linking dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/r/sidecar-canary

metrics-bot: ALERT: runtime.sidecar.request_latency.p95 > 350ms for cluster=canary (started 2026-03-17T14:12Z) :rotating_light:

Tomas: what specifically changed in the sidecar config? envoy filter? backoff? Any feature flags? can you paste the manifest or the helm values for the rollout?

Maya: deploy-bot: deploy v2.3.1-sidecar-config applied to canary by @Maya
Maya: the change was a small tweak to the downstream connection pooling and enabled `prefer_http2` in the sidecar. helm values snippet below:
```yaml
sidecar:
  prefer_http2: true
  connection_pool:
    max_connections: 400
    idle_timeout_ms: 30000
```

Priya: support: receiving a ticket from a customer (TICKET-1147) saying generation calls occasionally time out on our hosted API. customer provided a minimal repro (python requests, single-thread) that reproduces higher p95. repro gist: https://gist.github.com/example/repro-1147

Li: can we get a quick flamegraph or p95 distribution by route and kernel? run `rkctl query-metrics --cluster canary --route /generate --percentiles p50,p90,p95,p99 --since 1h` and attach traces. also capture sidecar logs with debug for a few minutes: `kubectl -n runtime logs -l app=sidecar -c envoy --tail=200`

Maya: attaching recent envoy tail (filtered):
```
[2026-03-17T14:18:01Z] debug upstream reset reason: connection failure (NO_ERROR)
[2026-03-17T14:18:02Z] info stream frozen, head-of-line blocking detected, queued_requests=12
[2026-03-17T14:18:02Z] warn pooled connection idle expired, opening new connection
```

Tomas: looks like connection pooling is thrashing under the new pool settings causing intermittent queuing at the sidecar. hypothesis: prefer_http2 changes connection lifecycle so pooled connections are closed more aggressively leading to head-of-line effects on bursty workloads. can we do a quick canary bisection: revert the `prefer_http2` flag on half of the canary nodes (cohort B) and compare p95 between cohorts A (unchanged) and B (reverted)? If p95 drops for cohort B that's a smoking gun.

Maya: doing it now — rolling cohort B (50% of canary) back to prefer_http2=false. will tag nodes with `group=b` and patch Helm release.

metrics-bot: UPDATE: cohort B (group=b) p95 dropped back to ~130ms within 3 min. cohort A still ~410ms. Details: https://dash.redwood.internal/r/sidecar-canary?split=group

Priya: confirmed repro against cohort B — TICKET-1147 customer test now shows baseline latency. I'll update the ticket that a partial rollback fixes it and we plan full rollback.

Carlos: are any dedicated or private customers impacted? we should triage customer comms.

Maya: no reports from dedicated/private — only canary cluster. rolling full rollback now and opening a rollback incident.

Li: next steps for postmortem: 1) add an e2e perf test for prefer_http2 path under bursty seq lengths, 2) add canary split by config flag so regressions are visible earlier, 3) instrument connection pool metrics (open, recycled, closed) at 1s granularity.

Tomas: also file a quick bisect checklist: 1) reproduce in canary 2) bisect by flag/helm values 3) capture flamegraphs + envoy stats 4) if bisect confirms, revert and hold release 5) ensure rollout gating includes p95 threshold check.

Maya: all set — full rollback completed. p95 normalized across canary. creating follow-up PRs for tests and metrics. tagging owners: @Li for instrumentation, @Tomas for rollout gating, @Maya for rollback runbook update. marking incident P2 and will write a short incident note.

metrics-bot: RESOLVED: runtime.sidecar.request_latency.p95 back below threshold for cluster=canary (resolved 2026-03-17T14:42Z) :white_check_mark:

Priya: I'll post the customer update and close TICKET-1147 once the postmortem is linked.

Maya: thanks everyone — we'll keep the follow-ups in a short postmortem doc and add the canary split config for future rollouts. :thumbsup:
